whatWeDo.title: What We Do?
whatWeDo.description:
Ambit advises founders, owner-managed businesses, and international groups on choosing and reviewing business structures aligned with commercial objectives, UK regulatory requirements, and tax efficiency. 
 Our advisory focuses on substance, not just registration. We assess how a business operates today, how it intends to grow, and the compliance exposure that arises from each structural option.

item1.title: Sole Trader
item1.description: A sole trader structure is often suitable for early-stage or low-risk activities. Profits are taxed under Self Assessment, with National Insurance obligations applying directly to the individual. While simple to operate, sole traders carry unlimited personal liability and limited tax planning flexibility as profits increase.

serviceSet.item1: Suitability of sole trader status based on income levels and risk profile
serviceSet.item2: Transition planning from sole trader to limited company
serviceSet.item3: Ongoing compliance and tax optimisation within Self Assessment

item2.title: Limited Liability Partnership (LLP)
item2.description: LLPs provide flexibility in profit allocation while offering limited liability protection. They are commonly used by professional practices, advisory firms, and joint ventures where commercial arrangements vary between members.

serviceSet.item2: Tax treatment of members and drawings

item3.title: Limited Company (Ltd)
item3.description: A limited company is a separate legal entity offering limited liability, structured governance, and advanced tax planning opportunities. It is suitable for growth-led businesses, contractors, property ventures, e-commerce operations, and investor-backed companies.

serviceSet.item1: Director remuneration strategies combining salary and dividends
serviceSet.item2: Corporation Tax planning and profit extraction
serviceSet.item3: Share structures for founders, investors, and employees
serviceSet.item4: Group structures and holding company arrangements

item1.heading: Why is choosing the right business structure important in the UK?
item1.body: The choice of business structure affects taxation, personal liability, reporting obligations, funding options, and long-term scalability. An incorrect structure can lead to higher tax exposure, compliance risks, and operational limitations as the business grows.

item2.heading: Can I change my business structure later?
item2.body: Yes. Many businesses start as sole traders and later transition to a limited company or LLP. Ambit advises on when and how to restructure to minimise tax exposure, manage compliance, and align with growth objectives.

item3.heading: How do I know whether a sole trader or limited company is right for me?
item3.body: This depends on factors such as income level, risk profile, growth plans, and tax efficiency. Ambit reviews your current operations and future plans before recommending the most suitable structure.

item4.heading: When is an LLP more suitable than a limited company?
item4.body: LLPs are commonly suitable for professional practices, advisory firms, and joint ventures where flexible profit-sharing and member arrangements are required. We assess whether an LLP or limited company best aligns with your commercial and tax objectives.

item5.heading: Do you advise international founders setting up businesses in the UK?
item5.body: Yes. Ambit advises international founders and overseas groups on UK business structures, regulatory requirements, tax exposure, and ongoing compliance obligations.

item6.heading: Do you provide only advisory, or also implementation?
item6.body: This page focuses on advisory services. However, Ambit also provides execution support, including company incorporation, registrations, accounting, tax compliance, and ongoing governance services.

item7.heading: How often should a business structure be reviewed?
item7.body: We recommend reviewing your business structure periodically, especially when there is revenue growth, international expansion, regulatory change, new investment, or exit planning.

item8.heading: How do I start a business structure review with Ambit?
item8.body: You can begin by requesting a business structure assessment. We will review your current setup, identify risks and opportunities, and provide clear recommendations.
